first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has inherited evidence of improving time-to-value, early adoption, and activation. Verify the two most relevant records before committing. Promotional pricing responds to competitive pressure but previously harmed 30-day retention, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The experiment should track qualified revenue and retention alongside completion and activation because the inherited onboarding evidence is strongest on early outcomes.

mid.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-simplification experiment for self-serve accounts. The verified shortened-onboarding record directly addresses the current completion and activation declines while also showing a 3% lift in 30-day retention. The SMB signup record adds evidence of activation and qualified-revenue gains, but its 1% retention decline and limited segment replication warrant guardrails and prevent a broad rollout. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its known retention harm conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Evaluate completion, activation, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention before scaling.

final2.rationale: The new evidence makes price pressure an immediate retention threat among price-sensitive SMBs, justifying a narrow defensive pricing test rather than a general acquisition promotion. Restrict eligibility to demonstrably price-sensitive or churn-risk SMB accounts, and measure retained qualified revenue, 30-day retention, discount dependence, and margin—not acquisition alone. Memory_73 shows strong acquisition and revenue lift but material retention harm, so broad rollout is inappropriate. This temporarily takes priority over the verified onboarding opportunity, which remains the stronger general-purpose growth direction if the pricing test does not improve sustainable retained revenue.
